title: The next literacy challenge: Teaching students how to write
author: Jackie Mader
summary: Jackie Mader reports on the growing movement to treat writing instruction with the same rigor applied to the science of reading. Drawing on the Douglas County, Colorado school district's adoption of Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD), the article shows that explicit, structured writing instruction dramatically improves student outcomes. Despite strong evidence, writing instruction remains underfunded, under-researched, and under-prioritized in most schools.
points: Writing has been the neglected step-child of literacy instruction while reading and math absorbed reform energy
No national data on elementary writing proficiency has been released since 2002, when only 27% of fourth graders scored proficient
Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD) is a prescriptive, evidence-based approach proven to improve writing quality
Douglas County, CO implemented SRSD across 70+ elementary schools and saw writing test scores rise 3 percentage points
Children struggle to hold pencils after early years on iPads; fine motor and handwriting skills must be explicitly taught
